newsitem.title: USA: CME live, feeder cattle end weak ahead of report.
newsitem.headline: CME live, feeder cattle end weak ahead of report.

text.p: CME live and feeder cattle futures closed weak ahead of the monthly USDA Cattle on Feed Report with weaker cash markets pressuring live cattle and higher corn futures weighing on feeders, traders said.

Live cattle closed 0.250 cent lower to 0.200 higher with February off 0.250 at 64.650 cents. Distant February set a new contract high of 69.750. Feeders finished 0.675 to 0.125 lower with March off 0.675 at 68.525. October and November posted new contract highs early before also turning lower.
Live cattle were pressured by a weaker than expected fed cattle trade this week and further weakness in boxed beef.

Packer demand is expected to be light next week after active fed cattle purchases this week, especially with beef prices looking very weak. Another cold front moving across the Midwest and heading east will likely keep beef movement down while cattle continue to put weight back on in the Southwest, traders said.
However, trading was mostly slow as the market awaited release of the monthly USDA Cattle-on-Feed report.

Estimates for the Cattle-on-Feed report pointed to on-feed supplies in the seven major states averaged 104.2 percent in a range of 102 to 105 percent of a year ago. December placements averaged 108.2 per cent in a range of 103 to 112 percent and marketings averaged 101.8 percent in a range of 99 to 107.1 percent of last year.

Feeder cattle remained under pressure from higher corn futures. Commission house selling touched off sell stops early under recent lows and prices held near lows as weakness in live cattle futures developed. Both of these factors may limit demand for feeders, traders said.
They noted that a higher CME feeder cattle index provided only light scale-down support early. The latest index was up $0.11 at $70.21 per cwt, the highest price level since March 9, 1995.
